\section*{Contenido completo depurado}

\subsection{Purpose}




This document converts the approved career strategy and CV positioning into a complete LinkedIn profile rewrite.




It includes:




\begin{itemize}
\item final headline recommendation;
\item 15 headline alternatives;
\item About section;
\item Experience rewrite;
\item Education rewrite;
\item Projects section;
\item Featured section order;
\item Skills ordering;
\item Creator/activity strategy;
\item recruiter keyword strategy;
\item availability and work-authorization wording;
\item future EU/Portugal/Germany wording;
\item sections to avoid or downplay.
\end{itemize}




This document is written in English because the target market is international remote work.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{1. LinkedIn positioning rule}




The LinkedIn profile must communicate one coherent identity:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
\end{mdcode}




It must not present separate unrelated identities such as:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Full-stack developer + AI engineer + 3D artist + game developer + researcher + designer
\end{mdcode}




Those areas can exist as supporting evidence, but not as equal headline identities.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{2. Final recommended headline}




Use this as the primary headline:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist | Unity WebGL, C#, CAD-to-Realtime Optimization, Technical Visualization
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Why this headline works}




It balances:




\begin{itemize}
\item role identity;
\item engine/tool keywords;
\item technical visualization niche;
\item recruiter-search keywords;
\item portfolio alignment with TwinSight X500;
\item enough specificity without overclaiming seniority.
\end{itemize}




It avoids:




\begin{itemize}
\item “Senior”;
\item “AI Engineer” as primary identity;
\item “Full-stack” as primary identity;
\item vague “multimedia engineer” wording;
\item generic “3D artist” positioning.
\end{itemize}

\section{4. LinkedIn About section}




\subsection{Recommended final version}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I build interactive real-time 3D systems for technical visualization using Unity, C#, WebGL and Blender.

My main project is TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. The project converts complex technical documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized interactive 3D experience with component selection, exploded views, cross-section tools, visual modes, technical UI, and usability/workload evaluation.

My strongest areas are:

- Unity / C# runtime interaction systems
- Unity WebGL deployment
- CAD-to-realtime asset optimization
- Blender-based technical asset preparation
- Interactive technical visualization
- Real-time inspection workflows
- Technical UI and documentation
- Python-assisted tooling and automation

I am currently completing my Multimedia Engineering degree at UNAD. I also completed advanced coursework in Electronic Engineering at Universidad Nacional de Colombia, which supports my technical foundation in mathematics, physics, systems thinking and engineering logic.

I am based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B roles in real-time 3D, Unity, WebGL, technical visualization, digital twin visualization, simulation, XR-adjacent development, and technical art workflows.

I also build secondary tooling prototypes with Python and LLM orchestration, including ARA Framework, a research automation prototype. I treat AI as a productivity and implementation assistant, while maintaining responsibility for architecture, integration, testing, technical judgment and final ownership.
\end{mdcode}

\section{13. Work authorization wording}




\subsection{For LinkedIn About}




Use:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I am based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B roles.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{For recruiter messages}




Use:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I am currently based in Colombia and can work remotely as a contractor/B2B provider. I do not currently hold EU work authorization, but I expect a future Portuguese passport in the medium term and may also have a Germany relocation route through family residence.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{For profile itself}




Do not over-detail the legal situation in the headline or first line.




Keep it simple:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Colombia-based · Open to remote contractor roles
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Do not say}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Authorized to work in the EU
\end{mdcode}




until legally true.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{14. Future EU / Portugal / Germany wording}




\subsection{Safe wording}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Medium-term EU mobility is strategically relevant due to an expected Portuguese passport and a possible Germany relocation route through family residence. Current availability remains Colombia-based remote contractor work.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Shorter wording}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Remote from Colombia now; EU mobility expected to become relevant in the medium term.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Avoid}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I can work in Europe.
I have EU work authorization.
I am relocating to Germany.
I am a Portuguese citizen.
\end{mdcode}




unless those are already legally true.

\section{17. Suggested first LinkedIn posts}




\subsection{Post 1 — TwinSight launch}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I recently completed TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.

The project explores how interactive real-time 3D can support spatial understanding of technical assembly processes.

Core features:
- component selection;
- exploded view;
- cross-section/clipping;
- visual inspection modes;
- technical information panels;
- CAD-to-realtime optimization;
- WebGL deployment;
- usability/workload evaluation.

The main idea behind the project:

Seeing parts is not enough. Users need to understand spatial relationships.

[portfolio link]
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Post 2 — CAD-to-realtime note}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
One of the main challenges in TwinSight X500 was converting CAD-derived drone geometry into assets suitable for real-time WebGL inspection.

The goal was not to preserve every raw CAD detail. The goal was to preserve component identity, assembly relationships and inspection clarity while reducing geometry enough for browser deployment.

That required:
- cleanup;
- retopology decisions;
- UV preparation;
- asset grouping;
- real-time material planning;
- Unity integration;
- interaction-aware optimization.

This is the kind of technical problem I want to keep working on: real-time 3D systems that make complex technical information easier to understand.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Post 3 — AI disclosure / workflow}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I used AI-assisted workflows during parts of the TwinSight X500 development process.

The useful part was not replacing technical judgment. It was accelerating implementation, debugging, documentation and research.

The responsibility still remained human:
- architecture decisions;
- integration;
- testing;
- validation;
- technical tradeoffs;
- final ownership.

For me, AI is most useful when it works as an engineering assistant, not as a substitute for understanding the system.
\end{mdcode}

\section{20. Profile photo guidance}

\begin{itemize}

\item no heavy filters;

\item good lighting;
\item simple clothing;

\item low-resolution images.
